tong2026audio: Large audio-language models understand acoustic content well but struggle with fine-grained reasoning such as event order, repetition, and duration, and current post-training relies on costly labels. Audio-Zero turns unlabeled audio contrast pairs into a self-play odd-listener game: the model describes what it hears as clues and identifies which listener heard a subtly different variant, yielding verifiable rewards without annotation. Trained on Qwen2-Audio-7B and Qwen2.5-Omni-7B, the method improves fine-grained reasoning on TREA, MMAU, and MMAR while retaining broad audio understanding, with finer auditory descriptions emerging under game pressure.
xiong2025thinking: Large audio-language models reason poorly under complex acoustic conditions and cannot call acoustic tools such as noise suppression, source separation, or temporal alignment. Thinking-with-Sound equips them with audio chain-of-thought, letting the model actively analyze and manipulate the audio signal through multimodal reasoning instead of treating audio as a static input. On a new perturbation-based benchmark, MELD-Hard1k, state-of-the-art models lose over half their accuracy, while the framework raises absolute accuracy by 24.73 percent for small models and up to 36.61 percent for larger ones, improving robustness without retraining.
sun2025audiomotionbench: Whether audio-language models can perceive the spatial motion of sound sources has remained untested. AudioMotionBench is a controlled question-answering benchmark built on binaural audio that asks models to infer the direction and trajectory of moving sources. Experiments show that current models average below 50 percent accuracy and cannot reliably recognize motion cues or directional patterns, exposing a systematic deficit in auditory spatial reasoning. The benchmark provides a diagnostic tool and a baseline for future work on spatial cognition in audio-language models.
bi2024lpnl: Applying large language models to graph learning is hindered by the sheer volume of information in large graphs. LPNL frames link prediction as natural-language reasoning: it describes graph details in prompts, uses a two-stage sampling pipeline to extract relevant subgraph information, and applies a divide-and-conquer strategy that keeps input tokens within limits. A T5 model is then fine-tuned with self-supervised link-prediction objectives. On large-scale heterogeneous graphs, the framework outperforms strong baselines, showing that LLMs can perform scalable link prediction without ingesting entire graphs.
bi2025context: Language models must stay faithful to retrieved context, yet alignment methods target values and intent rather than context adherence. Context-DPO is a direct-preference optimization method built specifically for context-faithfulness, paired with ConFiQA, a benchmark that simulates retrieval-augmented generation under knowledge conflicts. Using faithful and stubborn responses generated from ConFiQA as preference pairs, it aligns models to follow provided context. Across popular open-source models it improves context-faithfulness by 35 to 280 percent while preserving general generation quality and offering interpretable insight into context use.
bi2025decoding: In-context editing is the most effective knowledge-editing method but remains a black box, and its gains are undermined by stubborn parametric knowledge. DeCK analyzes token-level logits and finds that edited knowledge boosts logits yet competes with stale memorized facts. At decoding time it contrasts the next-token distribution produced by the edited context against that from the unedited parametric model, amplifying the new knowledge. Applied to Llama3-8B-Instruct on MQuAKE, it raises edited-fact accuracy by up to 219 percent and can be plugged into any in-context editing method as a training-free decoding component.
bi2025is: Factuality enhancement methods reduce hallucination by strengthening parametric knowledge, but this may make models ignore the input context. The paper revisits such methods, first verifying their effect on factual accuracy and then testing their impact on knowledge editing and context-faithfulness. Across methods, improvements in factuality are inconsistent, while context-faithfulness drops sharply by as much as 69.7 percent. Hidden-state and logit analyses trace the decline to overconfidence in memorized knowledge, showing that making models more factual is not a free lunch and that future methods must protect context adherence.
bi2026parametersvscontext: When retrieved context conflicts with parametric knowledge, language models cannot reliably decide whether to trust their parameters or the passage. CK-PLUG introduces Confidence Gain, a metric that detects such conflicts from entropy shifts in token probabilities after context insertion, and then adjusts the distribution of tokens with negative confidence gain through one tuning parameter. This gives fine-grained, plug-and-play control over knowledge reliance. On counterfactual retrieval scenarios with Llama3-8B, it sweeps memory recall from 9.9 to 71.9 percent around a 42.1 percent baseline while keeping text fluent and accurate, and improves general retrieval-augmented tasks.
bi2026promptcd: Most alignment happens at training time and needs costly labeled data, while contrastive decoding has been limited to narrow capabilities. PromptCD turns contrastive decoding into a general test-time behavior controller: for a target behavior it builds paired positive and negative prompts and contrasts the model responses, in token-level probability distributions for language models and visual attention maps for vision-language models, to reinforce the desired behavior. Requiring no extra training, it improves helpfulness, honesty, and harmlessness on large language models and strengthens behavior-consistent visual grounding and VQA accuracy in vision-language models.
bi2026reward: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards largely targets single domains such as mathematics, and purely online training restricts exploration. RGR-GRPO uses rubrics to supply both dense reward signals and offline guidance during GRPO training, letting models explore a wider solution space across domains. Across 14 benchmarks it beats methods relying only on outcome rewards or offline guidance, improving over the verifiable online RL baseline by 7.0, 5.4, 8.4, and 6.6 percent on math, physics, chemistry, and general reasoning. It keeps entropy stable during off-policy training and yields better pass@k, reflecting sustained exploration beyond current limits.
cai2020learning: Human motion prediction is hard because of the complex structural dynamics of body behavior. The method uses a transformer with global attention over temporally encoded joint sequences to capture long-range spatial correlations and temporal dependencies. A progressive-decoding strategy then predicts joints from the body center outward along kinematic chains, and a memory-based dictionary stores global motion patterns from training to guide prediction. Evaluated on Human3.6M and CMU-Mocap, the approach outperforms prior state-of-the-art methods on challenging motion prediction benchmarks.
cai2021unified: Motion prediction, completion, interpolation, and spatiotemporal recovery each demand different input constraints, so prior work builds separate architectures. A unified conditional variational autoencoder treats any input as a masked motion series and learns to sample missing regions from a distribution conditioned on the observed parts. Action-Adaptive Modulation injects semantic style guidance across the whole sequence, and cross-attention links encoder and decoder features for realism. On Human3.6M and CMU-Mocap the single framework produces coherent, style-controlled motion across all four tasks.
